newsitem.title: CANADA: Micrologix active on institutional trading.
newsitem.headline: Micrologix active on institutional trading.

text.p: Shares in Micrologix Biotech Inc inched higher on Tuesday on a large block trade to institutional investors on Tuesday, crossed by Yorkton Securities, the company and a Yorkton analyst said.
"Both the buyers and sellers were Canadian institutions," said Yorkton analyst Ezra Lwowski. "The buyers were both new and existing shareholders."
Micrologix, a Vancouver-based biotechnology firm, rose 0.15 to 3.55 on almost 2.4 million shares. Yorkton Securities traded a block of more than 2.3 million shares among its investors.
This block totals close to 13 percent of Micrologix's outstanding shares, company controller Art Ayres said.

Micrologix, which is in pre-clinical stages of its agents which target drug-resistant bacteria, had done a private placement of common share warrants with Yorkton Securities in September 1994, he said. The warrants expire September 21, Ayres said. Shareholders who sold the stock wanted to

maintain their present holdings instead of exercise the warrants and increase their stake, he said. "It's really an opportunity to increase institutional representation (through new buyers) in the company."
Micrologix was the third most actively traded issue on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Tuesday.
